title: Patients and clinicians managing patellofemoral pain should not rely on general web-based information
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 40 websites offering information on patellofemoral pain (PFP), retrieved from Google and Bing. Each content domain was rated against the International Patellofemoral Pain Research Network consensus statements as Accurate / Partially accurate / Inaccurate-Misleading / Not mentioned, and the share of websites in the 'Inaccurate/Misleading' category is reported per domain (definition of PFP 20%, clinical examination 15%, manual therapy 15%). That is item-level falsity against an external ground truth, so CONTENT.

estimates.country: searches performed in Melbourne, Australia (English-language websites; 20% of included sites had .com.au domains)
estimates.platform: Google and Bing search results (general web-based information)
estimates.measure_type: % of PFP websites whose description of the definition of patellofemoral pain was rated inaccurate/misleading against the international PFP consensus statements
estimates.value_raw: Misleading/inaccurate information ... in the definition of PFP (20% websites) [denominator 40 websites]
estimates.denominator: 40 unique active websites about PFP (first 20 results for each of 'patellofemoral pain' and 'knee cap pain' on each of Google and Bing = 80 URLs, minus 30 duplicates, 6 not PFP-specific and 4 inactive)
estimates.definition: The website's content on the definition of PFP was labelled 'Inaccurate/Misleading description' (one of four labels: Accurate/Clearly described; Partially accurate/Description lacks clarity; Inaccurate/Misleading description; Not mentioned) when compared with the International Patellofemoral Pain Research Network consensus statements
estimates.misinfo_def: no formal definition of misinformation; falsity operationalised as "(iii) Inaccurate/Misleading description" relative to consensus statements, with the paper noting "poor and inaccurate content may lead to ineffective or harmful decision-making from patients related to their healthcare"
estimates.source_quote: Misleading/inaccurate information was most commonly found in the deﬁnition of PFP (20% websites) and clinical examination (15%).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent reviewers (MSR and SH) rated every website against the 2016 and 2018 International Patellofemoral Pain Research Network consensus statements (an explicit external reference standard); inconsistencies discussed to consensus; no kappa or other reliability statistic reported. Protocol pre-registered on PROSPERO (CRD42018088671).
estimates.moderator_quote: The first 20 websites from each search (patellofemoral pain and knee cap pain) for each database were included for data extraction and analysis (n = 80). This decision was based on the assumption that the general public are more likely to read the sites that appear on the top of the list, and to ensure feasibility. ... Accuracy of PFP-speciﬁc content were based on the most recent consensus statements on terminology, clinical examination and treatment from the International Patellofemoral Pain Research Network published by an expert panel of clinicians and researchers.
estimates.notes: The paper reports NO overall 'share of websites containing any inaccurate information'; every accuracy figure is domain-specific on the same 40 websites. I extracted the single highest and headline domain (definition of PFP, 20%), which the abstract itself flags as where misleading/inaccurate information was 'most commonly found', to avoid stacking several overlapping rows built from the same 40 sites (see missed_or_uncertain for the others). breadth=misleading because the label merges 'Inaccurate' with 'Misleading'. denom_selection=curated (rank-truncated top-20 per search). COUNTRY CALL FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: the content is general English-language web material, but the search was run in one city with location data off, and the authors treat the locale as a validity limitation ('Comping our search in one city (Melbourne, Australia) may affect external validity'); I coded Australia/single on that basis, and Global/global would be the alternative.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Other domain-specific inaccuracy shares on the same 40 websites were not given their own rows to avoid multiplying overlapping estimates from one sample: clinical examination 15%, manual therapy 15%, and the Discussion's approximations ('information about these interventions is inaccurate or partially accurate in ~20% of websites', 'few websites provide accurate information regarding clinical examination (15%) and appropriate interventions (~15%)'). An adjudicator who wants per-domain rows should add clinical examination (15%) and manual therapy (15%) as further CONTENT rows on n=40. (2) Partially-accurate shares (hip/knee exercises 63%, foot orthoses 44%) belong to the middle 'lacks clarity' category, closer to QUALITY, and were not extracted. (3) '22% of websites recommended knee surgery for people with PFP' is a treatment-recommendation share, contrary to evidence but not coded as inaccurate by the authors, so no row. (4) Accurate-content shares (terminology 87.5%, definition 42.5%) are the complement side and must not be inverted (R8). (5) Credibility items (43% did not mention their source, 48% did not say if peer-reviewed, 38% no authorship, 58% no author qualifications, 35% no date, 50% no funding disclosure, 45% created to advertise products) are transparency/QUALITY indicators, not veracity, so no rows. (6) Exact numerator counts are not printed in the text (figures only), so value_raw carries the stated percentage rather than a count.

rob.design: Cross-sectional web content analysis, PROSPERO-registered (CRD42018088671); frame = first 20 results for 'patellofemoral pain' and 'knee cap pain' on Google and Bing, searched in Melbourne in February 2019 with history/cookies/cache cleared, location data off and no user account (80 URLs, 40 unique active PFP-specific sites analysed); two independent reviewers rated credibility items and PFP content against the 2016/2018 international consensus statements, disagreements resolved by discussion; no inter-rater reliability statistic reported; single-city search and English-only, top-20 truncation acknowledged as limitations.
rob.item6_quote: Each of the above-mentioned topic was labelled by the two reviewers according to 1 of 4 categories, as follows: (i) Accurate/Clear described; (ii) Partially accurate/Description lacks clarity; (iii) Inaccurate/Misleading description; (iv) Not mentioned.
rob.item10_quote: From the 80 URLs initially included, 30 were duplicates, six contained content not speciﬁc to PFP, and four were inactive, leaving 40 unique URLs for evaluation (Fig. 1). ... Domains with high rates of misleading/inaccurate information were deﬁnition of PFP (20%), clinical examination (15%) and manual therapy (15%).
